story.conflict: A daughter must decide what contact she wants without accepting her mother's claim that loving her stepfather requires believing a false history.
story.hook: A woman found birthday cards from the father she thought had forgotten her. Her mother had hidden one for every year since she was eight.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF THE CARDS WERE HERS
story.premise: An adult woman finds fifteen years of birthday cards her mother hid from the father she believed had forgotten her.
story.punchline: This time, she would hear him for herself.
story.script: Eva recognized the handwriting before she read the names. The cards were in a shoebox behind the spare blankets at her mother's house. Fifteen envelopes, all addressed to her. The newest had arrived before her twenty-third birthday. Her mother reached for the box and said there was no point upsetting everyone now. Eva asked who everyone meant. Her mother said Paul had raised her, and finding another father would break his heart. Eva said she'd found birthday cards, not a replacement for Paul. Her mother said her father could have tried harder. Eva said she wanted to ask him about that herself. The cards didn't explain why he hadn't come to the door. They did explain why she'd never received a card. Her mother said she'd been protecting her from disappointment. Eva asked whether she'd been allowed to decide what to do with even one envelope. Her mother said she was being ungrateful. Paul came to the doorway and asked what had happened. Eva showed him the box. He said he'd never known about it. Her mother told him Eva wanted to call her father. Paul asked why she needed either of them to approve that. Eva took the newest envelope home. There was a telephone number inside. She still had questions that fifteen cards couldn't answer. So she dialed it. This time, she would hear him for herself.
story.twist: The unopened cards show that her father's silence was partly manufactured, but do not answer every question about his absence.

youtube.description: A daughter discovers the birthday cards behind her father's supposed silence and refuses to let anyone else answer for him.
youtube.title: Fifteen Birthdays Behind the Spare Blankets

story.conflict: A wife must reclaim her judgment when the supposedly neutral professional advising her is personally involved in the betrayal.
story.hook: Her husband admitted their marriage counselor was his affair partner. His wife had paid for six sessions in which that woman called her suspicions unfair.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF HER SUSPICIONS WERE FAIR
story.premise: A husband admits that their marriage counselor is his affair partner after his wife has paid for six sessions questioning her own suspicions.
story.punchline: She had stopped asking those two people whether she'd imagined the problem.
story.script: Nora looked at the notebook she'd brought to every appointment. Helen had told her to write: Stop assuming the worst. The counselor, Helen, asked whether she needed a moment. Nora asked when the affair had started. Her husband, Ben, said before they'd booked the first session. Nora asked whose idea counseling had been. His. Helen said she'd believed knowing Ben would help her understand their difficulties. Nora asked why that understanding had been kept from the person paying for it. Ben said he hadn't known how to choose between them. Nora said she'd thought they were working on their marriage, not presenting her case to the other woman. Helen asked them to keep the conversation constructive. Nora asked whether that instruction applied to lying through six appointments. Ben told her anger wouldn't help. She turned the notebook toward him and asked which parts he'd wanted her to believe about herself. He looked at Helen. Nora saw him do it. She closed the notebook. Helen said they still had twenty minutes left in the session. Nora said they could use them to explain things to each other. Ben reached for her hand. She moved it and stood up. Outside, she opened the notebook again. She crossed out Stop assuming the worst. She hadn't decided what came next for her marriage. She had stopped asking those two people whether she'd imagined the problem.
story.twist: The counselor's advice to distrust her suspicions was serving a secret relationship rather than the marriage the wife thought they were discussing.

youtube.description: A wife learns that the woman advising her to stop suspecting an affair has been involved with her husband all along.
youtube.title: The First Page of Her Counseling Notebook

story.conflict: An interviewer must choose between obeying his manager's private request and giving the applicant an honest assessment independent of her marriage.
story.hook: A boss wanted his wife's job interview rigged against her. She believed he was helping her get back to work after raising their children.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF THE INTERVIEW WAS HERS
story.premise: A manager tries to rig his wife's job interview against her while letting her believe he supports her return to paid work.
story.punchline: Helen opened her list of questions again. Peter waited outside.
story.script: Sam had the application open when his manager, Peter, came in. His wife, Helen, was applying at another branch. Peter said Sam should interview her normally, then tell her somebody stronger had applied. Sam asked whether he'd read her experience. Peter said the qualifications weren't the issue. She'd been home for twelve years. Earning her own money would make her harder to live with. Then Helen arrived carrying certificates and a list of questions about the role. She thanked Sam for seeing her. Peter had said he'd put in a good word. Sam asked Peter to let them talk. During the interview, Helen explained the courses she'd taken in the evenings and asked where her experience needed updating. She hadn't expected the family connection to get her hired. Sam asked whether she knew Peter had requested a rejection before the interview. She went quiet. Then she asked him to repeat exactly what Peter had said. Peter returned when Sam called him in. He said he hadn't wanted Helen embarrassed by failing. Helen asked why he'd arranged the failure himself, then. Peter said they should discuss it at home. She said they could discuss their marriage at home. She wanted to finish her interview here. Sam hadn't promised her the job. He could promise the same assessment as the other candidates. Helen opened her list of questions again. Peter waited outside.
story.twist: The manager's apparent help is an attempt to keep his wife dependent on his income without taking responsibility for refusing her.

youtube.description: A woman prepares for her first job interview in years, unaware her husband's good word was a request to reject her.
youtube.title: The Rejection Her Husband Arranged

story.conflict: A homeowner must reclaim his private space when his employer treats access to feed his cat as permission to host clients there.
story.hook: His boss took over his house for a company retreat. He'd been sent to a fake conference to keep him away.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF HIS HOME WASNT COMPANY SPACE
story.premise: A boss sends an employee to a nonexistent conference so he can hold a company retreat in the employee's house without permission.
story.punchline: Milo took the sofa. Adam finally sat beside him.
story.script: Adam reached the hotel and found no conference booked. His boss, Vince, told him to enjoy the room. Then a coworker called on video. Behind her was Adam's kitchen. She asked why he wasn't at the retreat. Adam drove home. A company welcome sign covered his house number, and clients were drinking coffee on his sofa. His cat, Milo, had been shut in the bedroom because a guest disliked cats. Vince had a spare key only because he'd offered to feed Milo. Adam asked him to gather everyone's things. Vince pulled him into the kitchen and said he was embarrassing the company. Adam asked when the company had bought his house. Vince said he hadn't thought Adam would mind if he got a hotel weekend out of it. Adam said he'd been told to attend training, not lend out his home. Vince offered to pay for a cleaner afterward. Adam asked whether the cleaner would also make it something he'd agreed to. His coworker said she'd thought this was company accommodation. Adam said it wasn't. Vince asked him to let the afternoon finish before they discussed it. Adam told the guests the retreat would need another venue. Vince returned the key last, asking what he should tell the clients. Adam said that was his business to explain. He took the company sign off his door and opened the bedroom. Milo took the sofa. Adam finally sat beside him.
story.twist: The guests believe the company owns the retreat house, while the supposed business trip was designed to keep its actual owner away.

youtube.description: An employee returns from a fake conference to find his employer hosting clients in his private home.
youtube.title: The Conference That Emptied His House
